prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-05-28. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.09 |
| Retained earnings       | -9,884M |
| Current liabilities     | 20,274M |
| Current assets          | 22,162M |
| Shareholders' equity    | -9,270M |
| Total liabilities       | 64,211M |
| Total assets            | 54,941M |
| EBIT / operating income | 2,554M |
| Revenue                 | 23,078M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-05-28, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported balance sheet shows deeply negative shareholders' equity and retained earnings, implying technical insolvency and a highly leveraged capital structure (total liabilities exceed total assets by ~17%). Although the current ratio is marginally above 1.0 and EBIT is positive, these do not offset the structural distress signals. An Altman Z-score constructed from the given inputs falls well below 0.5, consistent with CCC-range credits.
DECISION: CCC
(The rating is placed at the middle of the CCC band because modest positive operating income and liquidity provide limited cushion but do not alter the fundamental insolvency picture.)
